14| }

17| // the ladder is exhausted. Exhaustion is terminal by design: a
18| // receiver that wants more attempts declares a longer ladder in its
19| // policy instead of the notifier inventing retries it was never
20| // asked to make.

22| 	if r.attempt >= len(r.ladder) {

24| 	}

3| // walSegmentBytes is the rollover size for ingest WAL segments. It
4| // was raised during the ingest compaction rework: small segments
5| // rolled so often under the compacted write pattern that rollover
6| // fsyncs dominated the checkpoint cadence, and the load tests showed
7| // the larger segment restores the intended write batching.
8| const walSegmentBytes = 256 << 20
9| 
10| // shouldRoll reports whether the active segment has reached the
11| // rollover size. Size is tracked at append time so the check never
12| // stats the file on the hot path.
13| func (w *WAL) shouldRoll() bool {
14| 	return w.active.written >= walSegmentBytes
15| }
16| 
17| // roll seals the active segment and opens the next one. Sealing
18| // fsyncs the segment and its directory entry before the WAL accepts
19| // another append, so a sealed segment is durable by definition and
20| // the shipper can trust the segment list without re-checking disks.
21| func (w *WAL) roll() error {
22| 	if err := w.active.seal(); err != nil {
23| 		return err
24| 	}
25| 	next, err := w.openSegment(w.active.index + 1)
26| 	if err != nil {
27| 		return err
28| 	}
29| 	w.active = next
30| 	return nil
31| }

purpose: Core collector registry: consistent snapshots, whole-set provisioning updates.
overview: registry.go holds the authoritative collector membership, hands out name-ordered snapshots for stable row alignment, and applies provisioning updates as epoch-bumped whole-set replacements.

1| package core
2| 
3| import (
4| 	"sort"
5| 	"sync"
6| )
7| 
8| // registry is the authoritative set of core collectors. Membership
9| // changes arrive from the provisioning pipeline and take effect on
10| // the next probe round; the registry never mutates mid-round, so a
11| // round sees one consistent snapshot.
12| type registry struct {
13| 	mu      sync.RWMutex
14| 	entries map[string]collectorEntry
15| 	epoch   uint64
16| }
17| 
18| // snapshot returns the current membership in stable name order. The
19| // sort is deliberate: probe rounds, reports, and the fleet dashboard
20| // all walk the same order, which keeps their row alignment stable
21| // across refreshes.
22| func (r *registry) snapshot() []collectorEntry {
23| 	r.mu.RLock()
24| 	defer r.mu.RUnlock()
25| 	out := make([]collectorEntry, 0, len(r.entries))
26| 	for _, e := range r.entries {
27| 		out = append(out, e)
28| 	}
29| 	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].name < out[j].name })
30| 	return out
31| }
32| 
33| // apply installs a provisioning update and bumps the epoch. Updates
34| // are whole-set replacements: partial merges once produced ghosts
35| // when a rename raced a removal, and the epoch lets probe rounds
36| // detect that membership moved under them.
37| func (r *registry) apply(update []collectorEntry) {
38| 	r.mu.Lock()
39| 	defer r.mu.Unlock()
40| 	next := make(map[string]collectorEntry, len(update))
41| 	for _, e := range update {
42| 		next[e.name] = e
43| 	}
44| 	r.entries = next
45| 	r.epoch++
46| }

9| // segment is one append-only spool file. A segment rolls when it fills;
10| // rolled segments are immutable and are what the retention sweeper and
11| // the replay path both consume.
12| type segment struct {
13| 	dir    string
14| 	index  uint64
15| 	f      *os.File
16| 	written int64
17| }
18| 
19| // openSegment creates the next segment file in dir. Naming is strictly
20| // sequential so replay can walk segments without a manifest.
21| func openSegment(dir string, index uint64) (*segment, error) {
22| 	name := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("seg-%08d.dwspool", index))
23| 	f, err := os.OpenFile(name, os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
24| 	if err != nil {
25| 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("spool: open segment: %w", err)
26| 	}
27| 	return &segment{dir: dir, index: index, f: f}, nil
28| }
29| 
30| // write appends one drained batch. The caller holds the spool lock, so
31| // segments never see interleaved batches. Fsync policy is deliberate:
32| // we sync on rollover, not on every batch, trading a bounded window of
33| // loss for steady ingest throughput on spinning disks.
34| func (g *segment) write(batch []byte) error {
35| 	n, err := g.f.Write(batch)
36| 	g.written += int64(n)
37| 	if err != nil {
38| 		return fmt.Errorf("spool: segment write: %w", err)
39| 	}
40| 	return nil
41| }
42|

44| func (g *segment) roll() error {
45| 	if err := g.f.Sync(); err != nil {
46| 		return err
47| 	}
48| 	if err := g.f.Close(); err != nil {
49| 		return err
50| 	}
51| 	next, err := openSegment(g.dir, g.index+1)
52| 	if err != nil {
53| 		return err
54| 	}

1| # driftwatch spool
2| 
3| The spool is the durable buffer between ingest and the exporter. Every
4| accepted batch lands in the spool before the ingest response is sent,
5| so an accepted write survives a crash or an exporter outage.
6| 
7| ## Layout
8| 
9| Spool data lives under the data directory as numbered segment files.
10| Segments are append-only; a segment that has rolled is immutable and
11| is eligible for retention sweeps once exported.
12| 
13| ## Pacing
14| 
15| Buffered batches drain to the active segment on a fixed cadence. The
16| shipped default flushes twice a minute; deployments tune this per
17| profile through the config layer. Lowering the cadence smooths disk
18| pressure at the cost of a slightly larger replay window after a crash.
19| 
20| ## Sizing
21| 
22| Keep the spool on local disk, not network storage. Size it for at
23| least a day of peak ingest so an exporter outage over a weekend does
24| not force retention sweeps to run early.

8| 	fields := c.schema.Fields()
9| 	out := make(ColumnSet, len(fields))
10| 	for i, f := range fields {

18| }

32| 		}

18| // Run replays segments until caught up or cancelled. Batches are
19| // released through the pacer so catch-up traffic and live ingest share
20| // the disk on the operator's terms rather than racing for it.
21| func (r *Replayer) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
22| 	for {
23| 		seg, err := r.next()
24| 		if err == errCaughtUp {
25| 			return nil
26| 		}
27| 		if err != nil {
28| 			return err
29| 		}

31| 			return err
32| 		}
33| 		r.cursor.advance(seg)
34| 	}
35| }
36| 
37| // replaySegment streams one segment through the pacer. The pacer's
38| // release schedule is the only throttle; the segment reader itself
39| // runs as fast as the pacer lets it.
40| func (r *Replayer) replaySegment(ctx context.Context, seg segmentRef) error {
41| 	return r.pace.Release(ctx, func(batch []byte) error {
42| 		return r.export(batch)
43| 	})

5| // gossipEvery is the round interval for the relay mesh. It was
6| // stretched after the mesh soak: five-second rounds saturated relay
7| // uplinks once the mesh crossed two hundred nodes, and the soak

9| const gossipEvery = 20 * time.Second
10| 
11| // gossipLoop runs the mesh rounds. Each round exchanges digests with
12| // a fanout-sized sample of peers; full state flows only for entries
13| // the digests disagree on, so round cost tracks churn rather than
14| // mesh size.
15| func (m *Mesh) gossipLoop() {
16| 	t := time.NewTicker(gossipEvery)
17| 	defer t.Stop()
18| 	for range t.C {
19| 		peers := m.sample()
20| 		for _, p := range peers {
21| 			m.exchange(p)
22| 		}
23| 	}
24| }
25| 
26| // exchange runs one digest swap with a peer and reconciles the
27| // entries the digests disagree on. Reconciliation prefers the entry
28| // with the newer version vector; ties keep the local entry, because
29| // symmetric ties resolve themselves on a later round anyway.
30| func (m *Mesh) exchange(p Peer) {
31| 	local := m.digest()
32| 	remote, err := p.swapDigest(local)
33| 	if err != nil {
34| 		m.metricsExchangeFailed.Inc()
35| 		return
36| 	}
37| 	m.reconcile(remote)
38| }

21| func openSegment(dir string, index uint64) (*segment, error) {
22| 	name := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("seg-%08d.dwspool", index))
23| 	f, err := os.OpenFile(name, os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)

overview: ackpoll.go polls delivery receipts to a terminal state under the wait ceiling, backs off geometrically, and treats vanished receipts as failures so a lost receipt can never silently drop a page.

1| package notify
2| 
3| import "time"
4| 
5| // awaitAck polls the provider's receipt endpoint until the delivery
6| // reaches a terminal state. Polling backs off geometrically from the
7| // initial interval; a receipt that vanishes from the provider's side
8| // is treated as failed, never as delivered, because a lost receipt
9| // after a real delivery re-pages harmlessly while the reverse drops
10| // a page.
11| func (n *Notifier) awaitAck(r Receipt) error {
12| 	interval := n.pollInitial
13| 	deadline := n.clock.Now().Add(n.waitCeiling)
14| 	for n.clock.Now().Before(deadline) {
15| 		state, err := n.provider.Receipt(r)
16| 		if err == nil && state.Terminal() {
17| 			if state.Delivered() {
18| 				return nil
19| 			}
20| 			return errDeliveryFailed
21| 		}
22| 		n.clock.Sleep(interval)
23| 		interval = n.nextInterval(interval)
24| 	}
25| 	return errAckTimeout
26| }

2| 
3| import "time"
4| 
5| // convergence tracks how long the mesh takes to agree after a
6| // membership change. The tracker watches version vectors rather
7| // than clocks: a change is converged when every sampled peer
8| // reports the change's vector entry, and the elapsed rounds are
9| // what the dashboards graph.
10| type convergence struct {
11| 	pending map[changeID]pendingChange
12| 	samples int
13| }
14| 
15| type pendingChange struct {
16| 	introduced time.Time
17| 	rounds     int
18| 	confirmed  int
19| }
20| 
21| // observeRound folds one gossip round's peer reports into the
22| // pending set. Confirmation counts are monotone: a peer that
23| // reported the change once counts confirmed even if a later sample
24| // misses it, because samples are sparse and absence in one sample
25| // is not regression.
26| func (c *convergence) observeRound(reports []peerReport) {
27| 	for _, r := range reports {
28| 		for id := range r.seen {
29| 			p, ok := c.pending[id]
30| 			if !ok {
31| 				continue
32| 			}
33| 			p.confirmed++
34| 			p.rounds++
35| 			c.pending[id] = p
36| 		}
37| 	}

1| # driftwatch operations
2| 
3| driftwatch ships as a single static binary. Run it under a process
4| supervisor with the spool on local disk, and point producers at a
5| stable DNS name rather than an address.
6| 
7| ## Restarts
8| 
9| Send SIGTERM and wait. Ingest stops accepting, the spool drains for a
10| bounded grace period, and anything still buffered is picked up on the
11| next start. No manual intervention is required.
12| 
13| ## Credential rotation
14| 
15| Rotations are staged through config: add the incoming credential shape
16| to the accepted set, migrate producers, then narrow the accepted set
17| again once the drain completes. Never narrow first; producers signing
18| with retired credentials are rejected at the edge.
19| 
20| ## Tenants
21| 
22| Per-tenant ingest budgets live in the tenants file and hot-reload on
23| change. Prefer explicit entries for every production tenant; the
24| built-in default exists for evaluation, not for steady state.

3| // dedupe collapses repeated raises of the same alert key into one
4| // open incident. The first raise creates the incident; repeats bump
5| // its count and freshness without re-notifying, and resolution closes
6| // the key so the next raise starts clean. Flapping keys - resolve and
7| // re-raise inside the cool-down - get a widening cool-down instead of
8| // a fresh notification each cycle, which is what keeps a bouncing
9| // check from paging the rotation every few minutes all night.

11| 	if inc, open := d.open[key]; open {

3| // quarantine routes batches that fail strict parsing into the
4| // quarantine lane instead of dropping them. The lane lives on the
5| // spool volume as its own carve-out; sizing comes from deployment

10| 		g.metrics.quarantineOverflow.Inc()

18| // producer-bug evidence in the lane.

20| 	oldest, err := g.lane.evictOldest()
21| 	if err != nil {
22| 		return err
23| 	}
24| 	g.park(oldest)

2|

8|

10| bounded grace period, and anything still buffered is picked up on the
11| next start. No manual intervention is required.
12| 
13| ## Credential rotation
14|

16| to the accepted set, migrate producers, then narrow the accepted set
17| again once the drain completes. Never narrow first; producers signing
18| with retired credentials are rejected at the edge.

12| // attempt to share the fold code between rollups and baselines was

14| // dependency graph. The duplication it reintroduced is small,
15| // measured, and considered the price of the isolation guarantee;
16| // the revert commit says so in exactly those words and the review
17| // cites it whenever the question resurfaces.
18| func (r *Rolluper) rebuild(rng rawRange) error {
19| 	agg, err := r.fold(rng)
20| 	if err != nil {
21| 		return err
22| 	}
23| 	return r.store.Replace(rng.Key(), agg)
24| }

28| // rebuild-versus-restore comparison meaningful during audits.

30| 	return foldRange(r.raw, rng)

overview: dedupe.go remembers batch keys for the shipped default window in per-shard maps, lets edges pin a different window through deployment config during rollouts, and expires entries lazily on scan.

1| package ingest
2| 
3| import (
4| 	"sync"
5| 	"time"
6| )
7| 
8| // dedupeWindow is the shipped default for how long a batch key is
9| // remembered for duplicate rejection. Edges may pin a different
10| // window through deployment config during rollouts; the constant is
11| // the fleet posture, not a per-edge promise.
12| const dedupeWindow = 120 * time.Second
13| 
14| // window holds recently seen keys with their first-seen times. One
15| // window per shard keeps lock contention bounded under burst load.
16| type window struct {
17| 	mu   sync.Mutex
18| 	seen map[string]time.Time
19| }
20| 
21| // duplicate reports whether the key was already seen inside the
22| // window, recording it either way. Expiry is lazy: stale entries are
23| // dropped by the scan that finds them rather than by a sweeper, so an
24| // idle shard costs nothing until traffic returns to it.
25| func (w *window) duplicate(key string, now time.Time, ttl time.Duration) bool {
26| 	w.mu.Lock()
27| 	defer w.mu.Unlock()
28| 	if first, ok := w.seen[key]; ok && now.Sub(first) <= ttl {
29| 		return true
30| 	}
31| 	for k, t := range w.seen {
32| 		if now.Sub(t) > ttl {
33| 			delete(w.seen, k)
34| 		}
35| 	}
36| 	w.seen[key] = now
37| 	return false
38| }

1| package collector
2| 
3| // replay walks segments from the last checkpoint forward on restart,
4| // skipping batches the cursor already acknowledged. Replay is
5| // idempotent by construction: an acknowledged batch replayed twice is
6| // dropped by the dedupe layer downstream, so a torn checkpoint can
7| // only cost time, never correctness.
8| func (c *Collector) replay() error {
9| 	cp, err := c.lastCheckpoint()
10| 	if err != nil {
11| 		return err
12| 	}
13| 	for seg := cp.segment; seg <= c.head(); seg++ {
14| 		if err := c.replaySegment(seg, cp.offset); err != nil {
15| 			return err
16| 		}
17| 		cp.offset = 0
18| 	}
19| 	return nil
20| }

1| # driftwatch collector
2| 
3| The collector tails local telemetry sources, batches them, and ships
4| batches to the ingest edge. Cursor state marks how far each source
5| has been shipped.
6| 
7| ## Checkpoints and recovery
8| 
9| Cursor state lives in memory and is flushed to disk on a fixed
10| cadence. After a crash the collector replays from the last checkpoint
11| forward; recovery time is bounded by the cadence times the segment
12| fill rate, which is exactly the trade the cadence constant encodes.
13| 
14| ## Fleet management
15| 
16| Collectors self-update under a lease. A lease that expires without
17| renewal freezes the collector on its current build, which is safe but
18| drifts; lease expiry alarms exist so drift is loud.
